title: White Mulberry: Ancient Silk Mulberries You Can Visit
meta_description: These trees were planted as machinery: white mulberry leaf is the only thing a silkworm will eat. Ten survivors of Europe's silk ventures.
intro: These trees were planted as machinery. White mulberry leaf is the only thing a silkworm will eat, so every ruler who fancied a silk industry ordered mulberries into the ground, and the trees stayed long after the venture folded. Christian IV tried it in Denmark, and the mulberry at Proviantgarden is the one tree from that royal scheme anyone can still point to. Maria Theresa's push put orchards across Taban in Buda, which is most likely where Budapest's oldest mulberry comes from, whatever the Ottoman legend says. Around Bergamo the leaves fed trays of larvae in farmhouse lofts, and three of those trees still stand in a public garden. Split's, in the courtyard of Hajduk's first ground, was DNA sampled in 2015 and cloned 105 times, once per year of the club. Nine cities so far, and every tree on this page is a leftover from an industry that failed.
